chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is it for the man that he should wash his head with the hibiscus (flower) before he shaves off his head?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should shorten it and wash it'.

key_terms.الْخِطْمِيِّ: Hibiscus flower, used here as a cleansing agent or for its scent during ritual washing

ai.seo_question: How should a man wash his head during ghusl when shaving or cutting hair according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the procedure for ritual purification of the head during *ghusl* after shaving, confirming that washing with *khittim* (a type of soap or plant extract) is permissible before or during the shaving process. This highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the use of cleansing agents, emphasizing that the essential requirement is the thorough washing of the hair and scalp to ensure ritual purity. The mention of *khittim* reflects the historical context of daily hygiene practices in early Islamic Medina, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual purification.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Aban Bin Taghlub who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is it for the man that he should wash his head with the hibiscus (flower) before he shaves off his head?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should shorten it and wash it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Mufaddal ibn Salih from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a person who wants to wash his head with marshmallow. He (the Imam) said, ‘He should shorten his hair, then wash.”’
